title: R1-M0-024 original protected Go TLS to Rust M1/M3/M4 route-observation once + same-VM A/B B/A
rationale: Task024 route/MTU hotpath cost. Existing source c203 original Rust autonomous M4 S2C calls observe_ipv4_route_mtu twice for one payload. Replace with original ProtectedScopedOwner sealed owner API which performs one fresh trusted route observation in same call and consumes original M1 slab/unique AEAD PN; unchanged raw driver still checks real kernel interface MTU and IPv4 DF. Historical 024 scoped reuse/10Hz clock evidence is preserved.

exact_changes.scope: new seal_normal_off_with_fresh_route_budget performs original owner active/Detached and validated kernel bound route+peer MSS budget once and original seal_normal_off_one in one call. Background Rust TUN TX no longer calls independent route observer followed by owner stale-route reobserve. Original external cached stale snapshot seal_normal_off_with_linux_budget retains live revalidation and fail-closed behavior. Original M4 ScopedRawIpv4Tx send_one still checks observed interface MTU per submission, uses IPv4 DF and kernel sendto; these are NOT yet optimized.

freeze A baseline333c1b3f, B source content git blob SHA3e0e4eec + fb00e4cb (exact code source c203), identical Go original TLS workload and runner. Two measurement actions, each its own two-leg ONE VM/job. Both directions same injected UDP app 10Mbps 64/256/1200 equal mix, fixed warmup10s measurement60s drain3s, no impairment.

Original Rust background test explicitly changes actual owned Linux namespace lo interface MTU 65536→1500 after original owner is Active and completed kernel traffic; new small S2C payload must be rejected by original M4 driver, TX successful count stays8, TX error rises, restore namespace MTU in cleanup. It does NOT claim automatic revalidation/recovery after MTU increase.

pinned_comparison.workload: Normal 1 lane, FEC off, original pinned protected Go TLS, same single Rust M1/M3/M4 real Linux raw/TUN, UDP app payload64/256/1200 equal count each direction logical10Mbps, 10s warmup+60s measure, 3s drain; no changed seed/queue/time to rescue failure
pinned_comparison.measured_CPU_scope: combined Go fixture, Go independent injector/receiver and original Rust owner all in one process; Rust thread CPU clocks not compared because A/B sample frequency differs; this is same-path development A/B, not full product CPU qualification

meaning: The owner-coupled route-once change has a strong reproducible >=18% delivered-normalized combined process CPU reduction on THIS bounded original Rust development data path, with no observed app integrity/p99 regression. Unlike previous storage-only <2% results, this is a meaningful measured same-VM AB/BA signal. It does not qualify the full product or maximum throughput, nor claim attribution of 18% to one syscall measured in D10; syscall counts are source-derived until diagnostic.
limits: Task024 is PARTIAL: every normal S2C packet still does one real kernel route lookup, original M4 raw send_one and raw recv_one_into still query interface MTU per packet; no netlink event-driven revision budget or recovery after MTU change.
All data still enters a global Rust registry mutex while AEAD and M4 raw sending, so true per-direction ownership/batch-ready<=32 and SPARSE/D10 C50 remain NOT_RUN.

Interface shrink regression proves the original M4 guard refuses a 52B S2C send on changed active loopback device. It does not prove outbound path PMTU events auto-revalidate or that a new snapshot is installed and delivery recovers.

Combined-process CPU includes Go fixture/injector/receiver. Not a full external SYN and fully native Rust client/server veth product cost measurement; same-host one-way application packet age p99 is not network RTT.

B01-B04 original production held async M4 driver, re-handshake external SYN, oversize automatic LINK fragmentation, production ABI feature gating and 500Mbps physical qualification remain NOT_RUN. Production V4 features0.
GitHub artifact ZIP digests are provider metadata receipts, binary SHA verified by native build/consumer. Scoped external cached-snapshot API retains same before-PN kernel recheck.
